compiled_state.title: As a DSO operator, the version-bump commit lands on the source branch as part of the reviewed PR diff, not on main outside the PR
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Modify `merge-to-main-pr.sh` to commit the version-bump on the source branch's HEAD before merge, so the version change ships as part of the reviewed PR diff rather than as a direct-to-main commit afterward. Resolve the design decision: whether the bump is made BEFORE final review (post-bump HEAD reviewed) or AFTER final review (with branch-protection re-review-dismissal accepted), and document the chosen sequencing.

**Why**: Today the version-bump commits directly to main outside the PR — this breaks subsequent `git pull origin main` on downstream worktrees and bypasses review on the bump itself.

**Scope**:
- IN: `merge-to-main-pr.sh` modification (version-bump on source-branch HEAD); design decision documented in the ticket comment thread; provenance trailer applied to the bump commit so S3's provenance check still skips integration review; sequencing relative to S4's RED-test-blocker check.
- OUT: Adding new versioning logic; release script (`release.sh`) modifications (separate concern); CI workflow naming for the bump check.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `merge-to-main-pr.sh` commits the version-bump on the source branch's HEAD before initiating the session→main merge. The version change appears as a commit in the reviewed PR diff, not as a post-merge direct-to-main commit.
  ← Satisfies: "merge-to-main-pr.sh commits the version-bump on the source branch's HEAD before merge"

- When this story is complete, the version-bump commit carries a provenance trailer (`DSO-Story-Merge:` or the coordinated trailer chosen by S1) so S3's `verify-session-provenance.sh` continues to recognize it as provenanced. Without this, S3 would flag the bump commit as unprovenanced and the integration review would re-fire — the exact regression S3 is supposed to prevent.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #3 (S5 provenance preservation)

- When this story is complete, the version-bump commit is sequenced relative to S4's RED-test-blocker check such that the bump cannot reintroduce a RED marker AFTER the check passed. Either S4 runs as the final required check AFTER the version-bump, or S5's bump is restricted to files that cannot match `.test-index` entries. The chosen sequencing is documented in the doc-story's ADR.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #3 (sequencing)

- When this story is complete, the design decision is recorded in the ticket: (a) bump-BEFORE final review (post-bump HEAD is reviewed; review is performed against the final state) OR (b) bump-AFTER final review (branch-protection re-review-dismissal is accepted; review must re-run on the post-bump commit). The chosen path is implemented and documented.
  ← Satisfies: "the S5 story includes the explicit design decision documented in the ticket"

- When this story is complete, sub-PR commit history shows version-bump on source branch (verifying SC4(b)'s history-audit verification).
  ← Satisfies: "sub-PR commit history shows version-bump on source branch"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done requirement

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Existing tests for `merge-to-main-pr.sh` (test-merge-to-main-pr.sh, test-merge-to-main-pr-thread-resolution.sh, etc.) cover the current direct-to-main commit path. They MUST be updated or extended to assert the new source-branch commit path.
- [Compatibility] The local-mode (merge.strategy=direct) version-bump path in `merge-to-main-direct.sh` is OUT of scope for this story — but should be considered for consistency in a follow-up.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

comments.body:
DESIGN_DECISION: bump-BEFORE-final-review

**Chosen path**: Insert pre-merge phase _phase_source_branch_version_bump that commits the version-bump on the source branch (session/...) HEAD BEFORE PR creation/update. Review fires against the post-bump HEAD (review-against-final-state).

**Rejected alternative**: bump-AFTER-final-review with branch-protection re-review-dismissal accepted. Rejected because re-review-dismissal undermines SC5(a)'s manual-review signal integrity — the epic is tightening review discipline, not weakening it.

**Rejected alternative**: two-PR pattern (separate version-bump PR). Rejected as premature abstraction (new branch prefix for one-line bump), conflicts with S1's single DSO-Story-Merge: trailer model, doubles CI cycles.

**Sequencing relative to S4's RED-test-blocker**: the version-bump touches ONLY the configured version file (e.g., VERSION or pyproject.toml). This file is never in .test-index (which maps source files to test files, not version-tracking files). Therefore S5's bump cannot reintroduce a RED marker AFTER S4's check passed, regardless of execution order. The check runs the same way on the post-bump HEAD as on the pre-bump HEAD.

**ADR cross-reference**: S_docs (cdc0-8cfc-38e6-4e7d) will record this as an ADR with full rationale linked here.
